title: The Rise of the AI Software Engineer: Jesse Han

primary.label: Coding Agents & Software Engineering
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 57%).

domains.label: Coding Assistants
domains.rationale: The talk introduces the Morph Code Index and Rift Coder 7B model specifically for building personal AI software engineers and coding assistants. The application vertical is IDE and software-engineering assistants. The product is announced as a new open-source index and model with a platform teased for early access, indicating a prototype phase.

summary: Jesse Han frames programming as an evolving discipline, noting that programming was once called "automatic programming" and predicting that engineering will one day be called "AI engineering." He envisions commanding legions of AI software engineers that understand codebases better than their human owners. Morph Labs' mission is to bring a personal AI software engineer to everyone—one that understands individual best practices, favorite idioms, and entire codebases, while evolving alongside the user and staying current. This personal AI software engineer would augment users across the entire software development lifecycle: ideation, specification, implementation, testing, and deployment. The major announcement is the Morph Code Index, a neuro-symbolic code database for users and their coding assistants. It combines static analysis, vector embeddings, and graph algorithms to create a code search index supporting natural-language semantic searches. It ships with a neuro-symbolic query language for precise results and makes entire codebases and git history visible to coding assistants via retrieval. Python bindings allow attachment to any coding assistant. The Code Index can also traverse codebases to generate training data, a pipeline already used to train Rift Coder 7B, described as the only open-source model for code editing that runs on a laptop and in an IDE. The Morph Code Index is open-source, transparent, and free, aligning with Morph Labs' belief that the future of software should belong to everyone. A platform for building, managing, and deploying personal AI software engineers is teased for AI Engineer attendees via waitlist.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Vision: The Rise of the AI Software Engineer
sections.summary: Jesse introduces himself and Morph Labs, framing programming as evolving from 'automatic programming' and predicting engineering will be called 'AI engineering,' with legions of AI software engineers writing code for humans.

sections.title: Mission: The Personal AI Software Engineer
sections.summary: Morph Labs' mission is to bring a personal AI software engineer to everyone—one that understands best practices, idioms, and the codebase better than the user, evolves with the code, and augments across the full software development lifecycle.

sections.title: Announcement: Morph Code Index
sections.summary: Jesse announces the Morph Code Index, a neuro-symbolic code database enabling semantic searches with natural language, making codebases and git history visible to coding assistants, and transmuting codebases into training data.

sections.title: Morph Code Index Features and Rift Coder 7B
sections.summary: The Code Index uses static analysis, vector embeddings, and graph algorithms for state-of-the-art code search, with a neuro-symbolic query language for precise results. Python bindings allow attachment to any coding assistant. The pipeline was used to train Rift Coder 7B, an open-source code-editing model that runs on laptops and in IDEs.

sections.summary: The Morph Code Index is open-source, transparent, and free. A platform for building, managing, and deploying personal AI software engineers is teased for AI Engineer attendees via waitlist.
